title: RAW UNREVIEWED: star-marker colour conditions a complete entry reading
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A red/yellow star beside an already admitted entry could mark a condition that changes the entry's asserted event or time, while the rival treats colour as graphic alternation and gives the same content reading regardless of colour. A candidate must give a complete reading of every nominated entry and its whole local continuation, fixing the colour rule and all word values before checking differently coloured entries on other physical folios. The older STAR_ENTRY_MARKER_COLOR family found no passing formal feature among 15 frozen features; this idea cannot reinterpret that failure as support. It needs an independently owned source relation tying visible marker colour to a concrete event or time and a stable entry-to-marker ownership map. Coloured stars, alternating phase, or a flexible gloss alone supply no semantic binding. No new page, reserve, or sealed data is proposed.

design.mechanism: A visible red/yellow star selects one fixed conditional semantic operator over a complete neighbouring entry and continuation.
design.unit: Complete marker-owned entries and their continuations on already admitted, exposed star pages, grouped by physical folio.
design.contrast: Colour-conditioned event/time reading versus the same complete word reading with colour as graphic alternation only.
design.prediction: If a source-independent event/time owner and entry-to-marker map are established, the conditioned model predicts a predeclared polarity or time change in every full red-versus-yellow entry pair while retaining fixed whole-word values and continuations; the graphic rival predicts no such directed change. Any unmatched complete entry or reversed phase must remain a counterexample, not receive a local repair. Currently the independent owner and meaning binding are absent.
design.scope: exploratory semantic proposal; no fixed test selected
